The v1→v2 release-review migration fixture proves removal of ancestry-bound reviewed_through_commit and requires an explicit fresh content-addressed reseal; the stale v1 digest is rejected, while v2 self-tests separately prove review-semantic changes alter the seal.

Public discovery verification now validates the explicit sitemap source contract in CI and, after same-SHA CI plus Pages deployment, probes the canonical published sitemap over HTTPS with redirects refused, bounded retries/size, XML parsing, canonical-host/path enforcement, duplicate rejection, and canonical-home presence before IndexNow notification.

CI and release-candidate workflows run branch validation through pull_request and push only on main, cancel superseded runs per PR/ref, and automatically execute canonical release readiness on accepted main instead of requiring an Owner manual dispatch.

Release acceptance is content-addressed: check-release-contract.py binds the exact tracked tree plus canonical review semantics through reviewed_content_digest, rejects the legacy reviewed_through_commit field, and carries an explicit v1 N−1 migration fixture that requires a fresh v2 reseal. product_outcome: Ship v0.4.2 as a bounded, fail-closed Codex whole-plugin selective-restore release from published v0.4.0: standalone-capable plugins are qualified with real provider MCP runtime evidence, while app-owned codex_app is explicitly PLUGIN_HOST_REQUIRED instead of being misreported as a standalone runtime. The candidate also removes ancestry-driven release-review reseal loops through content-addressed acceptance, moves runtime qualification before merge, deduplicates CI, automates accepted-main readiness, preserves ambient PluginStore denial, and retains the existing provider-state, Claude AGENTS, supply-chain, sitemap, tag and pre-publish hardening. The release harness also removes mutable-day tag coupling so passage of time alone cannot force a bookkeeping candidate mutation. Canonical tag-path validation now also owns version advancement and baseline chronology instead of relying on readiness transport. Protected tag creation now also minimizes the residual GitHub TOCTOU window by placing the final remote guard after provider checks. The release train also moves full provider/UI rehearsal before merge and makes that content evidence squash-portable, so accepted-main/tag phases no longer become the first observable correctness boundary solely because the commit SHA changed.

contract_evolution_review.rationale: The unpublished v0.4.1 Draft exposed two missing lifecycle boundaries and one review-reconciliation gap: legitimate pinned-provider state could make the next launch fail, Codex pre-tag runtime state was not followed by a clean relaunch, and a reviewer could inspect the Release workflow while missing a separate failed exact-tag CI run. Because these are release near-misses, v0.4.2 promotes durable runtime, evidence, tag-gate, CI lifecycle, and exact-tag pre-publish reconciliation controls rather than deleting state or relying on manual vigilance. The candidate also closes a public-discovery verification gap by promoting the sitemap from source-only checks to a same-SHA deployed canary before IndexNow notification. A second pre-tag near miss showed that a provider pin can add a new ambient instruction surface without a CLROOM code change: Claude 2.1.278 loaded an external ancestor AGENTS.md through built-in agents-md, so provider-version qualification now includes ambient-input-surface revalidation. Review also found that the first synthetic AGENTS artifact probe could pass on provider version preflight without executing its isolation assertions; v0.4.2 therefore requires an explicit launched-provider execution marker before that evidence can pass. Review of the first Claude AGENTS repair found a second correctness risk: using cwd as the boundary would block legitimate repo-root AGENTS on nested launches. The promoted control therefore binds the clean boundary to the nearest real Git worktree root, with nested-cwd negative and positive evidence at unit, launched-provider and exact-artifact layers. Final review also identified that an absence-only real-TUI confirmation could hide a provider walk that dropped all AGENTS instructions after encountering the denied ambient ancestor. The promoted TUI therefore proves both project instruction retention and external ancestor exclusion in one synthetic nested Git boundary. A local accepted-main qualification then exposed a fixture-level false blocker: the Claude AGENTS probe used a synthetic TMPDIR created under the ambient umask, while CLROOM requires its session projection temp root to be private. The probe now establishes and verifies mode 0700 before launch, and the provider-canary contract owns that fixture invariant. A subsequent accepted-main Codex pre-tag run exposed another release near-miss: the selected codex-app-tools MCP declaration was visible, but its provider-authored absolute launcher paths still targeted the sandbox-denied ambient PluginStore, so the real TUI reported codex_app failed with zero tools. The promoted control now rebases only in-bundle legacy MCP command/cwd paths into the shadow projection, machine-verifies the selected transport paths. Development System v2 then replaces that host-dependent acceptance target with a task-owned standalone MCP fixture whose real-provider initialize/tools-list boundary proves runtime capability rather than mere server-name visibility. The final accepted-main qualification also exposed a digest-transition lifecycle edge: a pre-fix CLROOM-owned projection marker used the legacy raw bundle digest, so the repaired binary could not safely clean it under the new semantic `.mcp.json` digest. Cleanup now recognizes that exact legacy ownership proof without allowing legacy projection execution, with tamper-negative coverage. Development System v2 additionally closes the release-harness incident itself: squash-invalidated ancestry seals are replaced by content-addressed review acceptance; dynamic runtime evidence remains outside tracked candidate bytes; duplicate branch/PR CI is removed; superseded runs are cancelled; accepted-main readiness is automatic. The codex_app zero-tools incident is reclassified from another path bug to a host-capability mismatch: app-owned codex_app is host-required, while standalone release acceptance is proven against a task-owned MCP fixture with real-provider initialize/tools-list evidence and an independent real tools/call protocol check. The real-provider harness also seeds trust only after a clean CLROOM-owned shadow is initialized and its ownership marker is verified, so Codex project trust is deterministic without scraping or answering the TUI trust screen. A final tag-gate review found that the tracked changelog date was incorrectly required to equal the future tagger calendar day. That action-time equality made passage of time itself mutate the accepted candidate boundary. The contract now makes time validation monotonic: one canonical declared changelog date may precede the real annotated tagger timestamp, future declarations fail closed, and both local and GitHub tag paths consume one checker. The same audit found that semantic-version progression was enforced by release-candidate readiness but not by the canonical release checker used at tag time. That transport-only ownership is removed: the checker now requires ACTIVE_CANDIDATE against the live published stable tag and anchors the changelog date at or after the published baseline date. The action-time ordering audit also found that remote main/tag/ruleset/baseline state was refreshed before slower provider checks, leaving a TOCTOU window before the irreversible protected tag push. The helper now places the final remote guard after provider checks and immediately before the single push, with the remaining non-atomic GitHub limitation documented rather than overstated. A final exact-head review also found that post-push tag reconciliation could collapse a failed remote read or a concurrent wrong/lightweight tag into an unsafe or misleading state. The helper now captures reconciliation status, queries both direct and peeled refs, preserves evidence on OUTCOME UNKNOWN, and distinguishes expected target, mismatch and verified absence. A second avoidable late escape in the v0.4.2 train then exposed a release-harness split-brain: CI qualification seeded synthetic Codex auth while the accepted-main pre-tag smoke created an otherwise equivalent temporary CODEX_HOME without auth and failed before its first clean MCP listing. This is treated as a HARNESS INCIDENT rather than a manual-auth prerequisite: the existing task-owned MCP fixture now centrally owns the private no-spend auth record for both paths, rejects conflicting state, and pre-merge contract coverage enforces the ordering and single-source invariant. The HARNESS INCIDENT review then found that the protocol's MOVE_LEFT_RUNTIME_EVIDENCE rule was not mechanically realized by the release scripts: both provider smokes required HEAD == origin/main and downstream gates keyed evidence to the accepted-main SHA. This made full runtime rehearsal structurally post-merge even when the exact PR candidate was locally observable. The repaired harness adds exact-PR rehearse mode, content-addressed evidence portability across squash, a Git-common-dir dynamic evidence store, and regression assertions that reject accepted-main-only rehearsal.
